rows.stem: ABCD is a parallelogram such that AF = 7 cm, FB = 3 cm and EF = 4 cm, length FD = equals
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - that E lies on BC and F is where AE crosses the diagonal BD (so AF, FE, FB and FD are pieces of those two lines) is shown only in the drawing of parallelogram ABCD; the stem names E and F without placing them. Page idx 6.
rows.solution:
E lies on BC, and the diagonal BD cuts AE at F. Since \(AD \parallel BC\), in triangles AFD and EFB we have \(\angle FAD = \angle FEB\) (alternate angles) and \(\angle AFD = \angle EFB\) (vertically opposite angles).

So \(\Delta AFD \sim \Delta EFB\) (AA similarity), and \(\dfrac{AF}{EF} = \dfrac{FD}{FB}\), that is \(\dfrac{7}{4} = \dfrac{FD}{3}\).

\(FD = \dfrac{21}{4}\) cm, which is option (A) \(\dfrac{21}{4}\) cm.

rows.stem: A circle centred at \((-1, 2)\) passes through the point \((0, 3)\). Radius of the circle is
rows.solution:
The radius is the distance from the centre \((-1, 2)\) to the point \((0, 3)\):

\(r = \sqrt{(0 + 1)^2 + (3 - 2)^2} = \sqrt{1 + 1} = \sqrt{2}\), which is option (B) \(\sqrt{2}\).

rows.subtopic: Nature of Roots and the Discriminant
rows.stem: If roots of the quadratic equation \(x^2 - k\sqrt{3}\,x + 2 = 0\) are real and equal, then value of k is
rows.solution:
Real and equal roots need the discriminant to be zero: \((-k\sqrt{3})^2 - 4 \times 1 \times 2 = 0\), that is \(3k^2 = 8\) and \(k^2 = \dfrac{8}{3}\).

So \(k = \pm\sqrt{\dfrac{8}{3}}\). Only the positive value is among the choices.

This is option (B) \(\sqrt{\dfrac{8}{3}}\).

rows.stem: Area of sector of a circle with radius 18 cm is 198 \(\text{cm}^2\). The measure of central angle is
rows.solution:
Area of a sector \(= \dfrac{\theta}{360^\circ} \times \pi r^2\), so \(\dfrac{\theta}{360^\circ} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 18^2 = 198\).

\(\dfrac{22}{7} \times 324 = \dfrac{7128}{7}\), so \(\theta = \dfrac{198 \times 7 \times 360^\circ}{7128} = 70^\circ\), which is option (A) \(70^\circ\).

rows.subtopic: Trigonometric Ratios of an Acute Angle
rows.stem: If \(2\tan A = 3\), then value of \(\sec A\) equals
rows.solution:
\(\tan A = \dfrac{3}{2}\), so \(\sec^2 A = 1 + \tan^2 A = 1 + \dfrac{9}{4} = \dfrac{13}{4}\).

A is acute, so \(\sec A = \dfrac{\sqrt{13}}{2}\), which is option (D) \(\dfrac{\sqrt{13}}{2}\).

rows.subtopic: Sum of First n Terms of an AP
rows.stem: In an A.P., \(a = -3\) and \(S_{17} = 357\). The value of \(a_{17}\) is
In the given figure, \(DE \parallel AC\) and \(DF \parallel AE\). Prove that : \(\dfrac{BF}{FE} = \dfrac{BE}{EC}\).
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - that D lies on AB and that F and E lie on BC (in the order B, F, E, C) is shown only in the drawing of triangle ABC; the stem names the parallels but not where D, E and F sit. Page idx 12.
rows.solution:
D lies on AB, and F and E lie on BC.

In \(\Delta BEA\), \(FD \parallel EA\), so by the Basic Proportionality Theorem \(\dfrac{BF}{FE} = \dfrac{BD}{DA}\) ... (i)

In \(\Delta BCA\), \(ED \parallel CA\), so by the same theorem \(\dfrac{BE}{EC} = \dfrac{BD}{DA}\) ... (ii)

From (i) and (ii), \(\dfrac{BF}{FE} = \dfrac{BE}{EC}\).

rows.subtopic: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
rows.stem: \(\alpha, \beta\) are zeroes of the polynomial \(p(x) = 3x^2 - 6x - 5\). Find the value of \(\dfrac{1}{\alpha^2} + \dfrac{1}{\beta^2}\).

rows.subtopic: HCF and LCM by Prime Factorisation
rows.stem: A trader has three different types of oils of volume 870 \(l\), 812 \(l\) and 638 \(l\). Find the least number of containers of equal size required to store all the oil without getting mixed.
rows.solution:
The least number of containers means the largest possible container, and its volume must divide each of 870, 812 and 638 exactly. So it is their HCF.

\(870 = 2 \times 3 \times 5 \times 29\), \(812 = 2^2 \times 7 \times 29\) and \(638 = 2 \times 11 \times 29\).

HCF\((870, 812, 638) = 2 \times 29 = 58\), so each container holds 58 litres.

Number of containers \(= \dfrac{870}{58} + \dfrac{812}{58} + \dfrac{638}{58} = 15 + 14 + 11 = 40\).

The least number of containers required is 40.

rows.stem: Prove that : \(\dfrac{1}{\sec x - \tan x} - \dfrac{1}{\cos x} = \dfrac{1}{\cos x} - \dfrac{1}{\sec x + \tan x}\)
rows.solution:
Since \(\sec^2 x - \tan^2 x = 1\), \(\dfrac{1}{\sec x - \tan x} = \dfrac{\sec^2 x - \tan^2 x}{\sec x - \tan x} = \sec x + \tan x\), and similarly \(\dfrac{1}{\sec x + \tan x} = \sec x - \tan x\). Also \(\dfrac{1}{\cos x} = \sec x\).

LHS \(= (\sec x + \tan x) - \sec x = \tan x\).

RHS \(= \sec x - (\sec x - \tan x) = \tan x\).

So LHS = RHS.

rows.stem: The perimeter of sector OAB of a circle with centre O and radius 5.6 cm, is 15.6 cm. Find length of the arc AB. Also find the value of \(\theta\).
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the stem asks for the value of \(\theta\) without saying what it is; only the drawing marks \(\theta\) as the angle AOB of the sector. Page idx 16.
rows.solution:
\(\theta\) is the angle AOB of the sector. The perimeter of the sector is the arc AB plus the two radii:

Length of arc AB \(= 15.6 - 2 \times 5.6 = 15.6 - 11.2 = 4.4\) cm.

Length of the arc \(= \dfrac{\theta}{360^\circ} \times 2\pi r\), so \(4.4 = \dfrac{\theta}{360^\circ} \times 2 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 5.6 = \dfrac{\theta}{360^\circ} \times 35.2\).

\(\theta = \dfrac{4.4 \times 360^\circ}{35.2} = 45^\circ\).

The arc AB is 4.4 cm long and \(\theta = 45^\circ\).
